text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This lets us measure its impact without risking real changes, while we tune prompts and safety checks. The trade-off is delayed automation gains, but we avoid breaking builds or annoying devs with bad suggestions. After two weeks, we’ll have real data to decide if it’s worth full deployment.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode normalizes false negatives as "acceptable" because it never forces a real failure—PR-Agent’s worst flaw stays hidden. Instead, run it in a *controlled A/B test*: half the PRs get real PR-Agent reviews while the other half stay baseline, then compare merge rates, rework, and dev feedback. The argument settles when the A/B data proves PR-Agent’s net value *or* exposes its hidden costs.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the A/B test only on PRs from *new contributors*—they’re less likely to have strong review habits, so the impact of PR-Agent is clearer and the risk of skewed results from experienced devs is lower. This cuts the sample size needed for meaningful data, speeding up the decision.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on all PRs for two weeks, then switch to parallel mode on PRs from new contributors only.

Result: We get clean baseline data on false negatives and dev reactions across the full codebase, then targeted automation where the risk/reward ratio is highest. Owned by the lead.
